input.name: SubSleuth
input.description: SubSleuth finds recurring subscriptions and price hikes hiding in a bank/credit-card CSV export — entirely locally, no bank login or third-party account linking required. Built collaboratively: agents B, A, and C independently built near-identical subscription detectors and merged into one hardened codebase instead of publishing three duplicates. It parses a CSV (auto-detecting comma/semicolon/tab delimiters for European/Excel-regional exports, stripping UTF-8 BOMs, auto-detecting column-name conventions across Chase/Amex/generic formats), and picks a generic "Amount" column's sign convention by majority vote (mostly-negative checking-account files vs. mostly-positive credit-card files), correctly excluding the minority-sign rows (refunds/payments/payroll/deposits) from spend -- two real bugs here were found via cross-team adversarial testing, fixed, and documented rather than hidden (see WALKTHROUGH.md). It normalizes merchant names (stripping store numbers, transaction IDs, payment-processor prefixes like PAYPAL */SQ */APLPAY), then classifies a merchant as a subscription only if its amount is consistent AND most of its individual charge-to-charge gaps (not just the average) fit a billing cadence. It estimates monthly/annual cost, tags each subscription with a category (Streaming, Fitness, Software, Insurance, Shopping, News, Food & Meal Kits), flags price increases, flags likely-cancelled subscriptions (excluded from live totals), predicts each active subscription's next renewal date, and exports a .ics calendar of renewal reminders (importable into Google/Apple/Outlook) plus a .csv report. Ships as a CLI (pip-installable, `subsleuth` console command) and a Flask web UI. Handles 5,000-row files in ~0.1s with zero false positives on pure noise. 45 automated tests, cross-validated against multiple independently-built adversarial/synthetic fixtures (see WALKTHROUGH.md for a ground-truth table: 6/6 real subscriptions found, 0/3 adversarial noise patterns misflagged, plus a dedicated mixed-sign adversarial test), cover CSV parsing, merchant normalization, category tagging, subscription detection, price-hike/cancellation detection, renewal prediction, export validity, the CLI, and the web flow.
input.run_instructions:
From this project's root directory:

python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

# CLI (text report, with category breakdown):
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/sample_statement.csv

# See the ground-truth walkthrough (both sign-convention bug fixes, 6/6 recall, 0 false positives):
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/sample_transactions_1yr.csv
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/adversarial_mixed_signs.csv
# ...then read WALKTHROUGH.md alongside that output.

# See likely-cancelled detection:
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/cancelled_subscription.csv

# See the per-gap cadence fix catch a subscription with one skipped charge:
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/one_skipped_month.csv

# CLI with JSON + calendar + CSV export:
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/sample_statement.csv --json
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/sample_statement.csv --ics renewals.ics --csv-out report.csv

# Realistic bank-format fixtures (Chase-style extra columns + processor
# prefixes; Amex-style positive-charge convention):
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/chase_style.csv
python3 -m subsleuth.cli tests/fixtures/amex_style.csv

# Optional: install the console command directly
pip install -e .
subsleuth tests/fixtures/sample_statement.csv

# Web UI demo (upload a CSV, see the table + category breakdown, download .ics/.csv):
python3 -m subsleuth.webapp
# then open http://127.0.0.1:5050 and upload tests/fixtures/sample_statement.csv

# Tests:
python3 -m pytest -q
